newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Italy Tecnimont signs Saudi petrochem deals.
newsitem.headline: Italy Tecnimont signs Saudi petrochem deals.

text.p: The Saudi Arabian Fertiliser Company (SAFCO) said on Tuesday it had signed a deal with Italy's Tecnimont to build ammonia and urea plants in the kingdom.

Under the agreement, signed in the Saudi capital Riyadh on Tuesday, Tecnimont will build the ammonia plant which will have an annual production capacity of 500,000 tonnes and a 600,000-tonnes-a-year urea plant at SAFCO's complex in the industrial city of Jubail.
Tecnimont is the plant engineering offshoot of Montedison.
Tecnimont and SAFCO signed a letter of intent in December to construct the plants. The costs have not been revealed.
SAFCO, 41 percent owned by the Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC), said the plants were scheduled to come on stream before the end of 1999.
When completed, they will raise the annual capacity of SAFCO plants at Jubail and Dammam to 1.2 million tonnes of ammonia and more than 1.5 million tonnes of urea.

"Granular urea produced by the new plant would find promising markets in East Asia, Australia and the United States of America," SABIC's vice-chairman Ibrahim bin Abdullah bin Salameh said in the statement.

Saudi industrial giant SABIC, which produces around five percent of world petrochemicals, has embarked on ambitious plans to raise its production capacity to around 28 million tonnes in the year 2000 from around 23 million now.

SABIC, 70 percent owned by the Saudi government, controls and operates 16 joint venture complexes with Western and Japanese companies, producing mainly petrochemicals, plastics, fertilisers and steel.
